text: What are the main building blocks of Flutter UIs?
explanation: Everything in a Flutter UI—layout, text, buttons, and padding—is built by composing immutable Widget objects.

text: Which widget should you try to use more often: StatelessWidget or StatefulWidget?
explanation: StatelessWidgets are simpler, lighter, and easier to maintain whenever a widget does not manage mutable local state.

text: What is the role of a BuildContext in Flutter?
answers: It locates a widget within the element tree
It compiles Dart code into native binaries
It replaces the State class in StatefulWidgets
explanation: BuildContext is a handle to a widget's position in the element tree, enabling lookups like Theme.of(context) and Navigator.of(context).

text: Which keyword declares a compile-time constant in Dart?
explanation: const values are evaluated at compile time and canonicalized in memory, whereas final values are set once at runtime.

text: What does the null-aware operator '??' do in Dart?
answers: Returns the right-hand value if the left-hand value is null
Throws an exception if a variable is null
Converts a nullable variable into a List
Checks whether two objects have the same type
explanation: The if-null operator (a ?? b) evaluates to a when a is non-null, and otherwise falls back to b.

text: What does the 'async' keyword on a Dart function indicate?
answers: The function returns a Future and can use await
The function runs automatically on a separate CPU thread
The function cannot throw any exceptions
The function executes synchronously before main()
explanation: Marking a function async enables the await keyword inside its body and wraps its return value in a Future.

text: How does Dart achieve true parallel execution across CPU cores?
answers: By spawning separate Isolates with their own memory
By marking every function with async
By sharing mutable global variables across threads
By using setState() inside a FutureBuilder
explanation: Dart Isolates do not share mutable memory; they communicate via message passing and can run concurrently on multiple CPU cores.

text: What is the purpose of a StatefulWidget?
answers: Render UI that does not depend on data
explanation: A StatefulWidget pairs an immutable widget configuration with a mutable State object that triggers UI rebuilds when data changes.

text: What happens if you change data in a StatelessWidget?
explanation: StatelessWidgets have no internal State object or setState() method, so mutating fields will not trigger a rebuild.

text: How should you update local state inside a StatefulWidget?
explanation: Calling setState() notifies the Flutter framework that the State object changed so it schedules a rebuild of the widget subtree.

text: Why is InheritedWidget fundamental to Flutter state management packages?
answers: It efficiently propagates data down the tree and rebuilds dependents
It persists app state to disk automatically
It replaces the need for BuildContext
It compiles state changes into SQL queries
explanation: Packages like Provider and Riverpod build on InheritedWidget's O(1) lookup and dependency registration to notify only listening widgets.
